raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

Small PRs often only need the CPU unit suite plus the tests of the module they touch. Today the CPU suite only runs as part of a full `run-ci` round, and `/rerun-group unit` is not a substitute: it expands to all ~1000 files under `test/registered/unit/`, dispatches the ~110 CUDA-registered ones to GPU runners, and its reply comment (~79 KB of commands) exceeds GitHub's 65,536-character comment limit.

## Modifications

- New `/run-cpu-ci` slash command (alias `/rerun-cpu-ci`). It dispatches a new `run-cpu-ci.yml`, which reuses `_pr-test-check-changes.yml` and `_pr-test-stage-cpu.yml`, so `base-a-test-cpu` is partitioned and run exactly as in PR CI (13 shards today, continue-on-error), with no `run-ci` label and no GPU stage. Intended usage for a small PR: `/run-cpu-ci` + `/rerun-group <module>`.
- The workflow is always dispatched on `main` with the PR head SHA as an input (fork and in-repo PRs alike), so the workflow definition is main's and only the code under test comes from the PR. That code runs on hosted runners with a read-only token and no inherited secrets, the same exposure as `/rerun-test` cpu mode. Gated the same way as `/rerun-test` (`cooldown_interval_minutes: 0` or write permission), plus the MIN_BASE_SHA pre-dispatch check.
- `_pr-test-stage-cpu.yml` gets a `skip_cache_save` caller input. A run on main's ref that executes PR code would otherwise save the HF / Rust caches under main's scope, where main and every PR restore them. `pr-test.yml` and `weekly-test-cpu.yml` don't pass it, so their behavior is unchanged.
- No prebuilt Rust extension artifact: its compile job runs on a self-hosted build node, so the stage falls back to its cache (about 7 min per shard on a cold cache).
- Docs: contribution guide, `ci-workflow-guide` skill, `.github/FOLDER_README.md`.

## Checks

- `py_compile`, pinned `isort` 7.0.0 / `ruff format` 0.15.1 / `codespell` clean; `actionlint` clean on the three changed workflows (it validates the `with:` keys against the local reusable workflows).
- Handler exercised against mocked GitHub objects: dispatch for write and cooldown-0 users (`ref: main`, `git_ref: <head sha>`), refusal for read-only users, the rebase gate, and a non-2xx dispatch; `/run-cpu-cl` gets a "did you mean `/run-cpu-ci`" hint.
- `compute_partitions.py --pr-test-yml .github/workflows/pr-test.yml` yields `base-a-test-cpu` with 13 shards, which the new workflow consumes.
- Not exercised: a real dispatch. `workflow_dispatch` needs the file on the default branch, so the first live run is a `/run-cpu-ci` comment after merge.

@@ -0,0 +1,69 @@
+# Runs only the per-commit CPU unit suite (base-a-test-cpu) against a PR head,
+# dispatched by the `/run-cpu-ci` slash command. A cheap check for small PRs:
+# pair it with `/rerun-group <module>` instead of a full `run-ci` round.
+#
+# Always dispatched on main, so the workflow definition and every reusable
+# workflow it calls are trusted; only the code under test comes from the PR.
+# That code runs on hosted runners with a read-only token and no secrets
+# (nothing here inherits them), the same exposure as `/rerun-test` cpu mode.
+name: Run CPU CI
+run-name: "[run-cpu-ci] ${{ inputs.git_ref }}"
+
+on:
+  workflow_dispatch:
+    inputs:
+      git_ref:
+        description: "PR head SHA to test"
+        required: true
+        type: string
+      pr_number:
+        description: "PR number (informational)"
+        required: false
+        type: string
+        default: ""
+      # Read by _pr-test-stage-cpu.yml via caller_inputs. Its fail-fast health
+      # check inspects sibling jobs of a pull_request run, which this is not.
+      skip_pr_test_health_check:
+        description: "Skip the PR test health check fail-fast"
+        required: false
+        type: boolean
+        default: true
+      # Also read via caller_inputs. This run is on main's ref, so a cache it
+      # saved would be restored by main and every PR, yet hold PR-written files.
+      skip_cache_save:
+        description: "Do not save the HF / Rust caches"
+        required: false
+        type: boolean
+        default: true
+
+concurrency:
+  group: run-cpu-ci-${{ inputs.git_ref }}
+  cancel-in-progress: true
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+  issues: read
+  pull-requests: read
+
+jobs:
+  # pr_test_yml stays pr-test.yml: compute_partitions.py reads it from the PR
+  # checkout, which may predate this file, and sizing shards off the per-commit
+  # stage's run_timeout_minutes keeps the split identical to PR CI.
+  check-changes:
+    uses: ./.github/workflows/_pr-test-check-changes.yml
+    with:
+      git_ref: ${{ inputs.git_ref }}
+      run_all_tests: true
+
+  # self_name must be the suite name: the stage passes it to run_suite.py.
+  # No rust_ext_artifact: its compile job runs on a self-hosted build node, so
+  # the stage falls back to its cache and compiles on a miss.
+  base-a-test-cpu:
+    needs: check-changes
+    uses: ./.github/workflows/_pr-test-stage-cpu.yml
+    with:
+      self_name: base-a-test-cpu
+      check_changes: ${{ toJson(needs.check-changes.outputs) }}
+      caller_inputs: ${{ toJson(inputs) }}
+      partitions: ${{ needs.check-changes.outputs.partitions }}
+      run_timeout_minutes: '15'

@@ -149,14 +149,15 @@ For CI to run on a pull request, it must have the "run-ci" label. Authorized use
 - `/run-extra-ci`: Extra CI **only**. Applies both labels, then reruns just `PR Test Extra`, leaving baseline CI runs alone. Use it when baseline is already green and you only need the extra tier.
 - `/rerun-test <test-spec> [<test-spec> ...]`: Reruns one or more specific tests directly. A spec may select a file, class, or method using `<file>::<TestClass>[.<test_method>]`. Multiple specs and file globs are supported. `--changed` (short form `-c`) adds every test file the PR itself adds or modifies (under `test/registered/` or the multimodal test directory), so a PR that touches several tests can rerun them all without listing them. Examples: `/rerun-test test_srt_endpoint.py`, `/rerun-test registered/core/test_srt_endpoint.py::TestSRTEndpoint.test_simple_decode`, `/rerun-test test_a.py test_b.py`, `/rerun-test test_*backend*.py`, `/rerun-test --changed`, or `/rerun-test -c`.
 - `/rerun-group <group> [<group> ...]`: Expands one or more registered test groups (for example, `/rerun-group rust-server`) and dispatches their tests through the same selective-rerun workflow. Groups are defined in [`scripts/ci/rerun_test_groups.json`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/scripts/ci/rerun_test_groups.json).
+- `/run-cpu-ci`: Runs only the CPU unit suite (`base-a-test-cpu`) against the PR head, partitioned the same way as in PR CI, without the `run-ci` label or any GPU stage. For a small PR, `/run-cpu-ci` plus `/rerun-group <module>` covers the unit tests and the affected module's tests. Alias: `/rerun-cpu-ci`.
 
 The rerun commands have the following permission rules:
 
 | Command | PR author | Other users | Additional rule for fork PRs |
 | --- | --- | --- | --- |
 | `/rerun-failed-ci` | Always allowed on their own PR | Must have `can_rerun_failed_ci` in `CI_PERMISSIONS.json` | None |
 | `/run-full-ci`, `/run-extra-ci` | Not auto-allowed -- these apply labels, which the PR-author allowance does not cover | Must have both `can_tag_run_ci_label` and `can_rerun_failed_ci` in `CI_PERMISSIONS.json` (every listed user has both) | None |
-| `/rerun-test`, `/rerun-group` | No special allowance; judged as any other commenter | Must have `cooldown_interval_minutes: 0` in `CI_PERMISSIONS.json`, or `write`/`admin` repository permission | None -- the same rule applies wherever the PR comes from |
+| `/rerun-test`, `/rerun-group`, `/run-cpu-ci` | No special allowance; judged as any other commenter | Must have `cooldown_interval_minutes: 0` in `CI_PERMISSIONS.json`, or `write`/`admin` repository permission | None -- the same rule applies wherever the PR comes from |
 
 <Warning>
 Selective reruns do not build or install a PR-local `sglang-kernel` wheel. If a PR changes `python/sglang/kernels/aot/` or code that depends on that AOT change, use the normal/full PR CI workflow. A `/rerun-test` or `/rerun-group` result may use the pinned released kernel and does not validate the combined change.

@@ -1635,6 +1635,80 @@ def handle_rerun_group(
     )
 
 
+CPU_CI_WORKFLOW_FILE = "run-cpu-ci.yml"
+CPU_CI_SUITE = "base-a-test-cpu"
+
+
+def handle_run_cpu_ci(gh_repo, pr, comment, user_perms, token):
+    """
+    Handles /run-cpu-ci: dispatch run-cpu-ci.yml, which runs only the CPU unit
+    suite (base-a-test-cpu) against the PR head, partitioned the way PR CI is.
+
+    Always dispatched on main with the head SHA as an input, for forks and
+    in-repo PRs alike, so the workflow definition is main's. It runs PR code on
+    hosted runners with no secrets, so it takes the /rerun-test gate.
+    """
+    if not _check_rerun_test_permissions(
+        gh_repo, pr, comment, user_perms, "run-cpu-ci"
+    ):
+        return False
+
+    allowed, gate_msg = _check_rebase_gate(gh_repo, pr, token)
+    if not allowed:
+        comment.create_reaction("confused")
+        pr.create_issue_comment(gate_msg)
+        return False
+
+    head_sha = pr.head.sha
+    ref = gh_repo.default_branch
+    try:
+        workflow = gh_repo.get_workflow(CPU_CI_WORKFLOW_FILE)
+    except Exception as e:
+        comment.create_reaction("confused")
+        pr.create_issue_comment(f"⛔ `{CPU_CI_WORKFLOW_FILE}` not found: {e}")
+        return False
+
+    dispatch_time = time.time()
+    resp = requests.post(
+        f"https://api.github.com/repos/{gh_repo.full_name}/actions/workflows/{workflow.id}/dispatches",
+        json={
+            "ref": ref,
+            "inputs": {"git_ref": head_sha, "pr_number": str(pr.number)},
+        },
+        headers={
+            "Authorization": f"Bearer {token}",
+            "Accept": "application/vnd.github+json",
+        },
+    )
+    if resp.status_code not in (200, 204):
+        print(f"Dispatch failed: {resp.status_code} {resp.text}")
+        comment.create_reaction("confused")
+        pr.create_issue_comment(
+            f"⛔ Failed to dispatch `{CPU_CI_WORKFLOW_FILE}`: {resp.status_code}"
+        )
+        return False
+
+    run_url = find_workflow_run_url(
+        gh_repo,
+        workflow.id,
+        ref,
+        "run-cpu-ci",
+        token,
+        dispatch_time,
+        pr_head_sha=head_sha,
+    )
+    target = f"`{CPU_CI_SUITE}` on `{head_sha[:12]}`"
+    if run_url:
+        pr.create_issue_comment(f"🚀 Running {target}: [View workflow run]({run_url})")
+    else:
+        pr.create_issue_comment(
+            f"🚀 Running {target}. Could not retrieve the run URL; check the "
+            f"[Actions tab](https://github.com/{gh_repo.full_name}/actions/workflows/{CPU_CI_WORKFLOW_FILE})."
+        )
+    comment.create_reaction("+1")
+    return True
+
+
 # Namespaces this handler owns. Anything else reaching the script is a comment
 # that merely quoted a path, and is left alone.
 OWNED_COMMAND_PREFIXES = ("/tag-", "/rerun-", "/run-")
@@ -1649,6 +1723,7 @@ def handle_rerun_group(
     "/rerun-test",
     "/run-full-ci",
     "/run-extra-ci",
+    "/run-cpu-ci",
 )
 
 # Removed commands, kept because they were documented long enough that muscle
@@ -1767,6 +1842,9 @@ def main():
     elif is_extra_ci:
         handle_run_extra_ci(repo, pr, comment, user_perms)
 
+    elif first_line.startswith(("/run-cpu-ci", "/rerun-cpu-ci")):
+        handle_run_cpu_ci(repo, pr, comment, user_perms, token)
+
     elif first_line.startswith("/rerun-failed-ci"):
         handle_rerun_failed_ci(repo, pr, comment, user_perms)
